text:
john_cust: Hey team — our Private inference fleet (in prod VPC) started getting connection resets to api.redwood.com yesterday evening. Users see intermittent ECONNRESET and TLS handshake timeouts when streaming.

olivia_support: Thanks — do you see this across all instances or a subset? Any recent firewall/NAT changes?

john_cust: It's across the autoscaling pool but only when traffic egresses through our NAT gateway. No config changes on our side that we know of.

sam_infra: Quick checklist: 1) are the VPC NACLs stateful or have explicit ephemeral port denies? 2) security group outbound allowing 1024-65535 ephemeral? 3) NAT gateway port exhaustion?

john_cust: Our NACLs were deployed with a narrower ephemeral range (1024-32767) intentionally. SG outbound is 0.0.0.0/0:443 allowed.

olivia_support: That NACL range could explain it — typical client ephemeral range goes up to 65535. If the NAT translates source ports and runs out, connections will fail with RSTs. Can you capture a tcpdump on an affected instance and on the NAT?

john_cust: Pasted what we grabbed from an app host when reproducing:

--- tcpdump snippet ---
14:12:03.123456 IP app-host.54321 > api.redwood.com.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
14:12:03.254321 IP api.redwood.com.443 > nat-eip.12345: Flags [R.], seq 0, ack 12346, win 0, length 0
--- end ---

john_cust: Notice the R from the cloud edge back to the NAT EIP.

sam_infra: That looks like NAT port exhaustion or a NACL deny on return path. Can you also paste VPC flow logs / NACL logs around the same times?

john_cust: Flow log: "REJECT" for src=api.redwood.com dst=nat-eip dstPort=12345 protocol=6 action=REJECT. NACL shows explicit DENY for ephemeral ports >32767 (we had a rule to limit ephemeral ports).

olivia_support: Bingo — NACL DENY on the return path. Even though SG is stateful, NACLs are stateless so you must allow ephemeral return ports explicitly. For Private inference we recommend allowing 1024-65535 outbound on NACL or at least up to 65535 inbound for ephemeral return.

jen_oncall: Quick mitigation steps: 1) add an ALLOW rule in NACL for ephemeral range (1024-65535) for TCP; 2) confirm order (lower-number rules first) and no conflicting DENY earlier; 3) if NAT port exhaustion suspected, scale NAT or use NAT gateway scaling / NAT instances with more ports.

olivia_support: Repro steps you can run to validate before/after:
- Run: sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host api.redwood.com and try a curl stream: curl -v https://api.redwood.com/stream
- Run: sudo conntrack -L | grep 443 to inspect active NAT entries
- Use: nc -vz api.redwood.com 443 from the app host (watch for immediate RST vs successful handshake)

conntrack-bot: conntrack snapshot: 443 entries: 1245 (threshold 1024) — warning emitted 14:11:58

john_cust: We updated the NACL to allow 1024-65535 and rolled a small test. Initial repro before change: curl timed out or reset in 40-60% of attempts. After change: streaming appears stable, no RSTs observed so far.

sam_infra: Great. Two followups: 1) remove overly restrictive NACL rules and prefer relying on stateful SGs for return traffic when possible, 2) monitor NAT metrics (ports in use) — if you see saturation, consider adding additional NAT gateways or using 1:1 EIPs per instance pattern.

olivia_support: I'll mark this thread with the recommended KB snippets and a short note for customers running Private VPCs: "Ensure NACLs allow ephemeral ranges for outbound TLS and confirm NAT port capacity."

john_cust: Thanks all — fix confirmed, will keep an eye on NAT utilization and report back if anything else shows up. :thumbsup:
